clue.text: Run, sometimes with companion

definitions.meaning: a run in a stocking or tights is a vertical line of unravelled stitches
a companion ... is the steep stairway leading down from a ship's deck

explanation.walkthrough: 'Companion' looks like a friend, but on a ship the companion is the hatchway and its stairway, the companion ladder.
explanation.definitionFit: Stocking runs are commonly called by this name in Britain, and a ship's companion stairway carries the same word.

clue.text: Harbour sought by immigrants

definitions.meaning: harbour as a noun means shelter or a safe refuge
describes the political protection refugees apply for in a new country

explanation.definitionFit: Political refuge granted to those fleeing persecution is the shelter newcomers apply for.

clue.text: Decide which one is to attract the crowd

parts.note: to attract a crowd is to draw it
lots can mean a great number of people, a crowd

explanation.surface: Someone must choose which performer will pull in the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'to attract the crowd' as the purpose of the choice; it is actually the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Settling who is chosen by picking straws or slips is the idiom of choosing by chance.

clue.text: Put money back in waistcoat after talk of cheque

indicators.note: after places the waistcoat word behind the cheque word

parts.note: cheque said aloud is check, and a check or restraint is a rein
vest is the American word for a waistcoat

explanation.surface: A banker tucks a cheque into a waistcoat pocket to pay it back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talk of cheque' asks for the word that sounds like it, check, and then its synonym, so one piece takes two steps.
explanation.definitionFit: To invest funds again, returning profits to the same venture, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Plenty of money to collect a bit of china

parts.note: pots of money is a colloquial phrase for a great deal of cash
to herd is to gather or round up

explanation.surface: A wealthy collector spends a fortune gathering pieces of porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' sounds like collecting antiques but is the verb herd, as in rounding up animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherd is a broken fragment of pottery, so the word means a shard of earthenware.

clue.text: Bishop putting pressure on marriage guidance

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
Relate is the British charity that offers marriage and relationship counselling

explanation.surface: A bishop leans on a couple to go for counselling.
explanation.walkthrough: RELATE is the UK organisation formerly called the Marriage Guidance Council.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior churchman such as a bishop or archbishop is a high-ranking cleric of that title.

clue.text: Odd individual

definitions.meaning: odd in the sense of peculiar or remarkable
individual in the sense of single, one only, as in grammatical number

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both strange and single, the grammatical opposite of plural.

clue.text: Carver needing a supply of plates

definitions.text: Carver needing a supply of plates

parts.words: Carver needing a supply of plates
parts.note: reads like someone carving a roast who needs dishes, but describes an artisan who cuts designs into metal printing plates

explanation.definitionFit: An artisan who incises designs into metal printing plates is described here by a dining-table image.

clue.text: The intimate secrets of a laundryman

definitions.text: The intimate secrets of a laundryman

parts.words: The intimate secrets of a laundryman
parts.note: private scandals one should not air in public, pictured literally as the soiled sheets a laundry worker handles

explanation.definitionFit: Washing soiled sheets in public is the idiom for exposing private scandal, so the phrase means embarrassing personal matters.

clue.text: Jelly diet many adapt

indicators.note: to adapt is to alter, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Many people adjust their diet to include jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jelly' is not dessert but gelignite, a jelly-like explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Gelignite is nicknamed jelly, and this is the related high explosive.

clue.text: Princess turned by love into an ass

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, shown as O

indicators.note: turned means the princess's name is written backwards

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters, a princess in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A princess is transformed into a donkey by love, fairy-tale style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' reverses REGAN to NAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild ass of Asia carries this name, so it is a specific kind of donkey.

clue.text: Ecclesiastical position following a chapter requiring faithfulness

indicators.note: following puts the church office after the a and chapter letters

parts.note: a curacy is the office of an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergy job comes after a chapter meeting that demands loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter' suggests a cathedral body but here is just C.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithfulness in the sense of fidelity to a source or original means exactness and precision.

clue.text: Ministry of Defence in changing times blowing its own trumpet

indicators.note: in places the defence ministry letters inside the rearranged word
changing means the letters of times are rearranged

parts.note: MOD is the abbreviation for the UK Ministry of Defence

explanation.surface: The defence ministry is boasting in these changing times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpet' suggests music, but blowing one's own trumpet is the idiom for boasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Boasting about oneself is lacking modesty, so the adjective describes a braggart.

clue.text: Club helping to provide part of food in emergency

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
a ration is an allotted portion, a helping

explanation.surface: A golf club helps hand out rations in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' is a golf club, IRON, and 'helping' is the noun meaning a portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers carry a small reserve pack of concentrated provisions for use when no other supplies exist.

clue.text: Makes up for stale cakes

parts.note: food that is off has gone bad or stale
cakes as a verb means hardens or solidifies, which is what something does when it sets

explanation.surface: Someone makes amends for serving cakes past their best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cakes' looks like a noun but is the verb, as mud cakes or cement sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Balancing or compensating for something is to counteract it, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Unglazed china in the rooms one shares

parts.note: a flat or matt finish has no gloss, like unglazed pottery
china is rhyming slang for mate, from china plate

explanation.surface: Unglazed porcelain is kept in shared lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so china is a friend, not porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: A person living in the same apartment, sharing its rooms, is described loosely here.

clue.text: Exceptional ale mixed with spice

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of ale and spice are stirred together into a new order

explanation.surface: A remarkable beer is brewed with added spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Special or particular, above the ordinary, is a slightly old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Herald with a warning to flee

parts.note: golfers shout fore as a warning to those ahead
to run is to flee

explanation.surface: A messenger with a warning tells people to run away.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's cry warning that a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald something is to come before it as a sign, which is to precede or anticipate it.

clue.text: Converse with one's counterpart on location

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after, so the location sits below the counterpart

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a colleague or ... number
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone chats with their opposite number at the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converse' looks like the verb 'to talk' but is the noun meaning reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The converse of something is its reverse, the thing facing it from the other side.

clue.text: Attention given advertisements for noise abatement aids

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
plugs are informal promotional mentions or adverts

explanation.surface: Ads that demand notice should come with something to block out the din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advertisements' gives PLUGS, the informal word for a promotional mention.
explanation.definitionFit: Small stoppers inserted into the ear canal reduce how much sound one hears.

clue.text: Changes one's opinions about time for spending plans

indicators.note: about means the opinion word goes around the time letter

parts.note: someone who budges shifts position or gives way in an argument

explanation.surface: A politician keeps shifting position on the timing of spending proposals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts BUDGES around T.
explanation.definitionFit: Financial schedules setting out planned expenditure are what a government or household draws up.

clue.text: Oddly spurn one whose existence is ignored

indicators.note: oddly signals that the letters of spurn and one are put together in a strange order

explanation.surface: Someone is strangely snubbed, as if they did not exist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for alternate letters, but it rearranges all of SPURN and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell coined the term in Nineteen Eighty-Four for someone erased from records, officially treated as never having lived.

clue.text: Severe test for gold share

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
to deal is to share out, as with cards

explanation.surface: A gold allocation proves a hard trial.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful or difficult experience that tests endurance is a trial of this kind.

clue.text: Having a branch over one's head

definitions.text: Having a branch over one's head

parts.words: Having a branch over one's head
parts.note: pictures sitting under a tree bough, but describes a stag or deer bearing branched horns

explanation.definitionFit: Bearing branching horns, as a stag does, describes the head with tine-like branches.

clue.text: So are writer's letters leaning to the right?

definitions.text: So are writer's letters leaning to the right?

parts.words: So are writer's letters leaning to the right?
parts.note: suggests a writer with right-wing sympathies, but describes slanted typeface or script

explanation.definitionFit: Sloping type, used for emphasis, leans to the right like handwriting.

clue.text: Record one preserves for those with refined tastes

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
to cure meat or fish is to preserve it

explanation.surface: A record of someone who makes jam, for the connoisseurs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' looks like jam but is the verb, as in curing bacon.
explanation.definitionFit: Gourmets devoted to fine food and drink are named after Epicurus.

clue.text: With nettles, spades may be unnecessary

parts.note: nettles as a verb means irritates, as needles does
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Gardeners with a nettle patch might find spades pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nettles' is the verb meaning annoys, not the stinging plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something serving no purpose is uncalled-for, a direct adjective synonym.

clue.text: Each foolish learner driver fails — no problem!

indicators.note: fails means the learner letter drops out of the foolish word

parts.note: silly means foolish
L is the learner plate on a British car

explanation.surface: Each foolish learner flunks the driving test with no trouble at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fails' removes one L from SILLY, leaving SILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without difficulty, as an exclamation, means it was effortless.
